summary: 6 nimmt! (Take 5) is a simple, cutthroat card game where players simultaneously play numbered cards into rows, trying to avoid being the one who takes a row full of penalty 'bull head' points. It's quick, laugh-out-loud mean, and scales well to large groups.
praised: Extremely easy to teach and quick to play
Good mix of prediction and luck
criticised: Can feel repetitive over many rounds
Little you can do about a bad hand

interaction.kind: simultaneous card reveal onto shared rows, forcing penalty cards onto whoever triggers a row
interaction.detail: All four number rows are shared board state that every player's card placement modifies, and playing (or being forced to play) the wrong number can hand a large penalty pile directly to you or, if you read the table right, steer it toward a rival. There is no private tableau at all — the shared rows are the entire game.
interaction.said: Long-running reputation as a 'mean' filler where you're 'trying to guess what everyone else will play' and can 'dump a whole row' on an opponent — explicitly tagged Take That.

scoring.how_you_win: Simultaneously play cards trying to avoid being the one who completes a row of 5 (taking its bull-heads); once someone's total penalty reaches 66 the game stops, and the player with the fewest accumulated bull-heads wins.
scoring.score_note: lowest penalty total wins; game ends once someone hits 66
